text: What if you had a whole law firm at your fingertips? Not a chatbot. A firm — with controls, and receipts.
You hand work to a firm, not a model. One request, in plain English — and unlike a chat window, everything that happens next is on the record.
The chief of staff delegates. Specialists pick it up. A risk review gets ordered — by the agents themselves. No invisible work: every handoff is a matter, with an owner.

And anyone can create a new agent — custom skills, connectors, and tools — shaped to your business, and your practice of law. Even the models are yours to swap: cheaper where it's routine, stronger where it counts.
Every agent runs on a budget it cannot exceed. Hard caps. Metered tokens. The spending stops before you get surprised.
Honestly? The deliverable is the least interesting artifact. Look at what's inside it: a conflicts notice the policy layer refuses to skip. Supervision, baked into the work.
And when anything tries to leave the building — it stops. A court filing, held for a human. Approve or reject. No exceptions, no override.
Underneath it all: a hash-chained receipt for every decision, verifiable offline. You don't trust the system. You check it.
Fully Open Source. For anyone to use and build. Take the entire OS, or just parts and make it your own. Bailey — by PossibLaw.
